title: AP College Football Poll Week 6: Top Risers, Fallers Unveiled in 2026 Rankings – Bleacher Report
body:
The Associated Press released its Week 6 Top 25 college football poll on Saturday, and the most dramatic movement came from the Missouri Tigers, who vaulted from No. 25 to No. 14 after a 45‑17 demolition of a formidable opponent. The surge not only validates the Tigers’ recent surge in form but also reshapes the mid‑tier landscape of the rankings, with several traditional powerhouses slipping and emerging programs taking advantage of the shifting hierarchy.

Missouri’s ascent was anchored by a dominant performance on the field Saturday, where the Tigers’ offense exploded for 45 points while the defense forced multiple turnovers and limited the opposition to just 17. Quarterback Connor Harlow threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns, while running back Malik “Lightning” Jones added 128 rushing yards and two scores. The comprehensive victory, coming against a top‑20 foe, gave voters a clear signal that the Tigers belong among the nation’s elite, prompting a 11‑spot jump that eclipsed the modest moves of most other teams.

The poll also saw notable declines. Ohio State, which had been perched at No. 5 after a string of high‑scoring wins, fell to No. 9 following a surprising 28‑24 loss to a struggling Iowa State squad. Meanwhile, Texas, long‑standing perennial contender, slipped from No. 8 to No. 12 after a lackluster defensive showing against a sub‑par Texas A&M team. These drops illustrate the volatility that can arise in a season where offensive fireworks often outweigh traditional defensive metrics in voters’ eyes.

Conversely, a handful of programs capitalized on the week’s outcomes to climb the ladder. The University of Southern California rose to No. 6 after a decisive 38‑14 win over Notre Dame, solidifying its return to national relevance under second‑year head coach Ryan Carter. North Carolina, previously unranked, entered the Top 25 at No. 24 thanks to a 31‑27 upset over Florida State, marking the ACC’s first new entrant in the poll this season. Such movements underscore the increasingly competitive nature of the 2026 campaign, where conference parity is more pronounced than in recent years.

Analysts attribute Missouri’s meteoric rise to a confluence of strategic adjustments and player development. Defensive coordinator Luis Ramirez shifted to a hybrid 4‑2‑5 scheme in the offseason, emphasizing speed and versatility, a change that paid dividends against the opponent’s spread offense. Offensively, the Tigers have embraced a balanced attack that leverages Harlow’s arm strength and Jones’s explosiveness, a combination that has kept defenses guessing. The Tigers’ recruiting class, ranked in the top ten nationally, is already making an impact, suggesting that this season could be a preview of sustained success.

Looking ahead, the Tigers’ newfound ranking places them squarely in the national conversation as they prepare for a crucial weekend clash with conference rival Kansas State, a game that could determine the Big 12’s championship trajectory. For the teams that fell, such as Ohio State and Texas, the next few weeks will be a test of resilience; a strong rebound could restore their standing, while further missteps may see them slip out of contention for the College Football Playoff. As the season progresses, the AP poll will continue to serve as a barometer of momentum, and Missouri’s dramatic climb illustrates how quickly fortunes can change in college football’s ever‑evolving landscape.
